title: Adaptive Token Budgeting and Pricing Modes — Design Spec
author: Asha Iyer
body:
Overview

Purpose: This design spec describes the Adaptive Token Budgeting subsystem and associated Pricing Modes to make per-route and per-tenant token economics flexible, predictable, and SLO-aligned. The goal is to enable customers and internal systems to select tradeoffs between latency, cost, and quality through an explicit budgeting API and backend billing primitives.

Scope:
- Config surface for routes and tenants to express token budgets and pricing mode.
- Runtime enforcement and accounting hooks in the serving runtime to decrement budgets and emit metrics.
- Billing integration that maps budget consumption to invoiceable units and credits.
- UI/Console representation and rollout steps.

Non-goals: internal-only rate limiting (existing quota system remains); deep ML model changes; user-facing experiments outside configured modes.

Background and motivation

Redwood currently charges primarily per-token and via reserved capacity contracts. Customers building latency-sensitive features request more predictable per-route economics tied to SLOs (e.g., 95th percentile latency < 120ms) and per-feature budgets (e.g., chat sessions capped at 1,000 tokens/day). Existing approaches are either too coarse (account-level token bundles) or too brittle (static per-request limits).

Adaptive Token Budgeting introduces:
- Explicit budgets that can be bound to a route, API key, or tenant.
- Pricing modes that change how budget consumption maps to billable tokens (flat token accounting, SLO-backed creditization, and hybrid subscription models).
- Runtime signals (latency, tail, error-rate, model fallback) to dynamically adjust effective spend rates to protect SLOs and cost targets.

Goals and success metrics

Primary goals:
1) Allow product teams and customers to declare per-route/tenant token budgets and pricing mode.
2) Ensure billing accuracy within 0.5% of serving accounting for budgets-enabled routes.
3) Reduce cost-per-request for bursty workloads by >= 12% via intelligent remapping (within 6 months of rollout).
4) Provide tooling to convert current token bundles into budgeting constructs with < 5% migration delta.

Success metrics (sample):
- Percentage of paid requests routed through a pricing-mode (target 30% in 6 months).
- Billing reconciliation delta (target <= 0.5%).
- Customer-reported latency regressions attributable to budgeting toggles (target < 1%).

High-level design

Components:
- Budgeting API (admin): /v1/budgets (create, update, delete, preview)
- Enforcement library: thin runtime hook inside the serving runtime to decrement budgets, consult pricing mode, and emit accounting events
- Pricing Engine: maps accounting events to billing line-items according to mode and rules
- Console: UI to visualize budgets, projected spend, and SLO impact
- Reconciliation service: asynchronous job that verifies usage events against billing tables nightly

Pricing modes (supported):
1) fixed_token: straightforward tokens-in/tokens-out pricing. Accounting event = tokens_consumed.
2) slo_credits: budgets are denominated in SLO credits. Credits are consumed at a variable rate based on runtime signal (e.g., high tail latency -> credit burn increases). Billing maps credits to invoiceable token-equivalents at periodic conversion.
3) buffered_subscription: subscription seat or capacity that provides a discounted effective per-token rate after a fixed monthly commitment; budget prevents overspend beyond allowed burst credits.
4) hybrid: per-route rules that mix modes (e.g., warm path fixed_token, cold path slo_credits).

Configuration model (example)

Config object (JSON example):
{
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions/preview",
  "scope": "route",
  "mode": "slo_credits",
  "budget_amount": 5000,            // units depend on mode (tokens or credits)
  "budget_period": "P1M",         // ISO 8601 period (monthly default)
  "slo_target": {"p95_latency_ms": 120},
  "fallback_policy": "throttle_then_fallback",
  "adjustment_policy": {"latency_threshold_ms": 150, "burn_increase_pct": 50}
}

Config table:
| field | type | description |
| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
| route | string | Route path or matcher |
| scope | enum | route|key|tenant |
| mode | enum | fixed_token|slo_credits|buffered_subscription|hybrid |
| budget_amount | integer | numeric budget for period in mode units |
| budget_period | string | ISO period for budget reset |
| slo_target | object | SLO target(s) used for adjustment decisions |
| fallback_policy | enum | allow|throttle|fallback| |
| adjustment_policy | object | Runtime adjustment tuning parameters |

Runtime enforcement and events

At request completion, the serving runtime will emit an accounting event to the Budgeting topic (Kafka):
- event fields: timestamp, route_id, tenant_id, api_key, tokens_input, tokens_output, model_variant, latency_ms, status, applied_mode, effective_budget_units_consumed

The Enforcement library behavior (pseudocode):
1) Lookup budget config by route/key/tenant precedence.
2) Evaluate adjustment_policy against observed signals (latency_ms, error_rate).
3) Compute effective_consumption = base_token_count * mode_multiplier (mode-dependent).
4) Atomically decrement budget; if insufficient, apply fallback_policy.
5) Emit accounting event and metrics (budget_remaining, burn_rate, last_adjustment).

Mode multipliers (example):
- fixed_token: 1.0
- slo_credits: variable (1.0 -> 3.0 depending on stress signals)
- buffered_subscription: 0.6 (discount factor) until subscription cap reached

API and Console UX

Admin API endpoints (surface):
- POST /v1/budgets  -> create or preview config
- GET /v1/budgets/{id} -> current state and projected spend
- PATCH /v1/budgets/{id} -> change mode/budget/fallback
- POST /v1/budgets/{id}/preview -> simulate N requests and report cost & SLO impact

Console screens:
- Budget Summary (percentage consumed, forecasted burn)
- What-if Preview (simulate different traffic shapes and adjustment settings)
- Billing Impact (translated to invoiceable units)

Telemetry and SLOs

Metrics to emit per budget-enabled route (prometheus names):
- redwood.budget_remaining{route,tenant,mode} gauge
- redwood.budget_burn_rate_per_min{route,tenant,mode} gauge
- redwood.budget_adjustments_total{route,tenant,policy} counter
- redwood.budget_denied_requests_total{route,tenant,reason} counter
- redwood.budget_accounting_delta{route,tenant} gauge (nightly reconciliation diff)

SLO contracts and enforcement policies (recommended defaults):
- p95_latency_ms <= 120 for latency-sensitive chat routes
- error_rate <= 0.5%
- budget_reconciliation_delta <= 0.5% monthly

Billing integration and invoice mapping

Mapping rules (examples):
- fixed_token: invoice line = tokens_consumed * token_rate
- slo_credits: invoice line = credits_converted * credit_conversion_rate (conversion window: daily close)
- buffered_subscription: base_monthly_fee + overage = (committed_tokens*discount_rate) + overage_tokens*standard_rate

Reconciliation and auditing

Nightly job responsibilities:
1) Aggregate accounting events and produce aggregate consumption per budget id.
2) Cross-check against billing ledger; compute budget_accounting_delta.
3) If delta > 0.5%, create an investigation ticket and tag affected customers.

Rollout plan

Phase 0 (pilot, 4 weeks):
- Internal pilot with platform routes only.
- Validation of enforcement hooks and event schema.
- Manual reconciliation checks.

Phase 1 (beta customers, 8–12 weeks):
- Onboard 3–5 customers across use cases (chat, embeddings, reranking).
- Enable only fixed_token and buffered_subscription modes initially.
- Provide migration tool to translate token bundles.

Phase 2 (SLO-backed modes, 12–16 weeks):
- Open slo_credits and hybrid mode.
- Monitor billing delta and tail latency.
- Add UI previews and automated conversion tool.

Phase 3 (GA):
- Full rollout, doc updates, and pricing page changes.
- SLA and support plan updates.

Migration and backward compatibility

- Existing token bundles: migration tool will compute an equivalent budget in fixed_token mode; customers can opt-in to change modes.
- Fallback: default to existing quota system when budget system is unavailable (circuit breaker).

Security, privacy, and compliance

- Budget configs considered customer metadata — include KMS-backed storage for sensitive fields.
- Accounting events contain no PII; API keys are hashed before being emitted to Kafka.
- Audit logs retained consistent with data-retention policy; include export path for compliance customers.

Operational runbook (short)

Common alert triggers:
1) budget_accounting_delta > 0.5% for > 24h -> paging to Billing SRE
2) budget_denied_requests_total spike -> page Platform Oncall (possible config bug)
3) nightly_reconciliation_job_fail -> page Data Platform

Quick recovery steps:
1) For mis-billed customer: run manual aggregate and create invoice credit; revert budgets if rollout caused regression.
2) For enforcement hotpath failures: toggle budgeting circuit-breaker for affected cluster; monitor error rates.

Security review checklist: handled (encryption at rest, encrypted audit trail, role-based UI access).

Open design questions and tradeoffs

- Conversion cadence for slo_credits -> invoiceable tokens (daily vs hourly).
- Precise conversion algorithm: linear vs tiered conversion rates under stress.
- UI UX: how much control to expose to customers for adjustment policy tuning.

Risks

- Misconfiguration could cause customer downtime (mitigation: preview + safeties).
- Billing reconciliation complexity increases (mitigation: nightly reconciliation and manual override).

Ownership and next steps

Owners:
- Product: Asha Iyer (spec lead)
- Engineering: Daniel Kline (runtime), Priya Nair (billing engine)
- SRE/Billing: Evan Zhou

Next steps (first 30 days):
1) Finalize event schema and enforcement library API.
2) Implement budget create/preview API and Console mockups.
3) Prepare pilot plan and select internal routes.

Appendices

Appendix A — Example CLI commands
$ redwood admin budgets create --route "/v1/chat" --mode slo_credits --budget 10000 --period P1M --slo.p95_latency_ms=120

Appendix B — Example accounting event (JSON)
{"timestamp":"2026-12-12T08:23:12Z","route":"/v1/chat","tenant_id":"acct_1234","tokens_input":12,"tokens_output":128,"latency_ms":98,"status":"ok","applied_mode":"slo_credits","effective_budget_units_consumed":64}

Appendix C — QA checklist
- Unit tests for enforcement library multipliers and atomic decrement
- Integration test with billing conversion job
- End-to-end simulation with what-if traffic shapes
- Console preview matches server-side projection within 2%
